articleTitle: Phase Method: A More Precise Beam Steering Model For Phase-Delay Metasurface based Risley Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A phase method is proposed specially for metasurface based Risley antennas, with which analytical solutions are obtained for both beam direction prediction and deflector orientation retrieval. The new method is compared with traditional paraxial approximation method to reveal their connections and differences. A phase-delay metasurface is simulated to verify the theoretical model. The prediction error of the phase method is only 1.2° at a large steering angle of 56°, and an improvement of 5.0° is achieved comparing with paraxial method. It is demonstrated that phase method is a more precise and appropriate method when phase-delay metasurfaces are utilized as deflectors in Risley antennas.

articleTitle: A Group-Sparse Compressed Sensing Approach for Thinning Multi-Carrier Frequency Diverse Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Frequency diverse arrays can achieve range-angle-dependent beampattern due to the change in frequency between the successive antenna elements. Using multi-carrier frequency diverse arrays can provide a higher degree of freedom that can be exploited to focus the transmitted energy in a small range-angle region by creating a dot-shaped beampattern. This letter proposes an algorithm based on group-sparse recovery and convex optimization for thinning multi-carrier frequency diverse arrays. The algorithm ensures that the turned off antennas have a negligible effect on the beampattern for all multi-carrier frequencies assigned to them. Numerical results showed that the proposed algorithm can save about 25% of the antenna elements compared to the existing synthesis methods under the required constraints on the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: 64 × 64 MIMO Antenna Arranged in a Daisy Chain Array Structure at 50 Gbps Capacity
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we advance the concept of a daisy chain array structure to create a 64 × 64 multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array that can maintain a 50 Gbps transmission rate in the whole azimuth without appreciable degradation. 64 independent subchannels for MIMO multiple transmission are achieved by pairing two elements for each subarray arranged in a dual-ring configuration. It is clarified that this remarkably high channel capacity is attributed to the two significant factors; an improved directivity due to an optimum in-phase excitation and low correlations between the subarrays caused by the orthogonal alignment of the array with respect to incident waves.

articleTitle: Analysis of Misalignment Effects on Link Budget of an Implantable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effects of lateral and angular misalignment on the link budget of a dual-band antenna operating at ultra-high frequency bands (1.64 GHz and 3.56 GHz) for usage in implanted medical devices. The antennas were simulated when located inside muscle tissue. Insertion loss and transmission efficiency for different misalignment conditions were examined. Based on simulation results, antenna performance is stable in the range of lateral misalignment of -20 mm to 20 mm, and angular misalignment of -90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> to 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>.

articleTitle: RF Cancellation of Coupled Transmit Signal and Noise in STAR across 1 GHz Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The shrinking spectrum availability has led to the development of creative approaches for spectrum allocation and reuse. A most promising approach for spectrum is the simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) scheme. A major challenge in realizing STAR is the coupling of high power transmit (Tx) signals into the co-located receiver, leading to strong signal interference in the operating frequency. In addition, to this direct interference, cancellation of harmonics and the transmit noise is also necessary. Overall, for successful STAR realization, 3 signal components must be suppressed, namely 1)Tx signal, 2)Tx signal harmonics, and 3)Tx noise. In this paper, we present the design of RF cancellation of these components across 1 GHz using antenna and filters. In addition, we also show the effect of Tx noise coupling in an array environment and means to suppress it.

articleTitle: Mathematical Formulation of Phase Retrieval for Phaseless Spherical Near-Field Antenna Measurements with Probe Correction
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This work describes a mathematical formulation for the computational phase retrieval for phaseless spherical nearfield antenna measurements. This formulation, based on the spherical transmission formula with probe correction, is implemented in a MATLAB programme PhaseMore.

articleTitle: A History of Leaky Waves and Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The history of leaky waves and leaky-wave antennas is an interesting one, with much of the theory being put on a firm foundation in the 1950s and 1960s by early pioneers such as Nathan Marcuvitz and Arthur A. Oliner. Rapid development of leaky-wave antennas took place after the foundation was established, and the development spread to areas such as printed-circuit technology, optics, and metamaterials. This presentation will review some of the basic history of leaky waves and leaky-wave antennas, and discuss some of the recent advances in the field.

articleTitle: Optimization of Beam-Steering Metasurfaces Using Modified Cross-Entropy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Strict phase and amplitude control of electromagnetic waves promises significant applications but it still remains a critical challenge. We present a simple, lucid yet versatile stochastic optimization approach to reduce the side-lobe level (SLL) in the radiation pattern of a beam-steering metasurface. The proposed algorithm is capable of efficiently handling computationally expensive electromagnetic (EM) problems. The efficiency of this method has been validated with numerical simulation results, which shows quick and optimal convergence.

articleTitle: Optimizing Amplitude Distribution in a Feed Array to Control Side-Lobe Levels of a Beam-Steering Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: An attempt to establish analogy between the antenna array pattern synthesis theory and the metasurface beam-steering control is presented in this paper. Beam steering has been achieved by using a phase transformation metasurface, and the side-lobe level (SLL) reduction has been achieved by optimizing the excitation amplitude of feed array. Optimization has been performed by a simple evolutionary approach based on cross-entropy (CE) method, and the results validate the efficiency of the algorithm, as well as verify the concept of SLL control using excitation amplitude manipulation.

articleTitle: Daisy Chain MIMO Antenna for Whole Azimuth Tens-of-Gigabit Connected Cars
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system that has the ability to perform beam scanning operation over the whole azimuth, with the aim of realizing vehicular communications at several tens of gigabits capacity. The developed MIMO antenna comprises 64 elements arranged in a dual-ring structure, like daisy chain flowers, named daisy chain MIMO antenna, with 32 subarrays by pairing two elements for each subarray in a rotational way, forming 32 independent subchannels for MIMO transmission, covering all angles toward the target of communication. The analytical results reveal that the proposed antenna system provides a channel capacity of more than 200 bits/s/Hz at the signal-to-noise power ratio (SNR) of 30 dB over the whole azimuth, which is equivalent to 20 Gbps for the bandwidth of 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Time-Modulated Reactive Elements for Control of Electromagnetic Energy
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Accumulation of electromagnetic field energy in classical passive structures such as resonators and reactive circuit elements is limited by the amplitude of time-harmonic external sources. In the steady-state regime, all incident power which is not absorbed is fully re-radiated (reflected), and the time-averaged stored energy is constant, even though the external source continuously supplies energy. Recently, we have shown that lossless objects can continuously accumulate energy if their properties are properly modulated in time. Here, we discuss this possibility and study means to release this accumulated energy in the desired moment or moments of time in form of pulses of the desired shape. Furthermore, we discuss a possibility of keeping the energy inside the load, turning off the incident wave and changing the modulation function of the load. Finally, instead of a single time-reactive element we consider a parallel time-varying LC circuit, that gives the same functionality, in addition allowing to engineer currents flowing through the load circuit elements.

articleTitle: Literature Review on Radar Absorbers using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper exhibits a literature survey on the subject of radar absorbing materials (RAM) to provide a general overview on working theory, absorber types, electromagnetic properties, and materials used for their design especially using metamaterials. Metamaterials as artificial structures owning unusual electromagnetic effects are discussed with the different possible applications like shielding, cloaking, etc. The recent developments in metamaterial absorbers are introduced along with different possible structures, operating frequency bands, and vital applications.

articleTitle: On the Availability of Processes for Creation a Thing Space from a Null Space
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The study in this paper is on the fundamental topological processes remaining at the background of any kind of event. Topological principles are presented with an approach submitted here first. The responce of the fundamental question here is correlated with the realizability and/or unrealizability by using the topological analysis approaches. An algorithm is formulated. We call Self-constructing Model by itself the Model achieved by the topological correlations of the algorithm. The model proves the occurence and/or creation of the processes for a compact and reliable development of any kind of events. The possible evaluation processes of a universe is structured with a topology of a thing space from a germ in a null space from that point of view by the use of convenient transition maps. The principal axiom of pure existence is builded in the generation of topological spaces that has a role in possible to generate thing space from null space. The topological mechanisms of anything structures are designed.

articleTitle: Power-dependent invisibility devices for antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Electromagnetic invisibility or cloaking represents one of the most important breakthroughs enabled by metamaterials and metasurfaces. Among its possible applications, cloaking of antennas has been emerged as a topic of particular interest since it increases the degrees of freedom available for the design of complex telecommunication platforms. In this contribution, we will show that the potentialities of cloaking for antennas can be further increased if we make use of power-dependent metasurfaces, i.e., textured engineered surfaces loaded with non-linear elements. We will show that such structures enable shaping the radiation pattern of an antenna array depending on the input or received power by the driven element.

articleTitle: Non-local power wave transformations using Omega Bianisotropic Huygens’ Metasurface Pairs
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Omega bianisotropic Huygens’ metasurfaces (BHMs) are subwavelength thin sheets that have been used in applications such as wide-angle reflectionless refraction of plane waves, and wideband matching between dielectric media. However, for the BHM design to be passive, reflectionless and lossless, the wave transformation is restricted to conserve local power at every point over the metasurface. For non-local power transformations, pairs of BHMs can be engineered, with a separation between them, to re-distribute the local power profile at will. This opens the possibilities to a multitude of wave transformations that conserve the global power, but not necessarily the local power at every point. This paper presents two non-local power transformations that are realized with a paired BHM configuration, namely beam expansion and beamforming.

articleTitle: Split-step wavelet propagation modelling using local operators
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The atmospheric long-range propagation above the ground is of major importance for many ground systems as radars. The split-step wavelet method allows to compute efficiently this propagation, using a matrix-vector product for the free-space propagation. In this paper we propose a local method for the free-space propagation based on library of propagators. From numerical experiments, we show that this new method is cheaper in terms of memory cost whereas the matrix-vector product solution yields faster computation time.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Circularly-Polarized Lens Antenna Operating at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A circularly-polarized (CP) lens antenna operating at 300 GHz is realized using a low-cost 3-D printer with high temperature resin. The CP antenna comprises three parts, a phase compensation lens, a dielectric grating providing a 90° phase difference between two orthogonal field components and a linearly-polarized feed horn. The antenna is measured using a near-field scanning system. Excellent agree between the simulated and measured radiation patterns is obtained.

articleTitle: Inflective Spaces: Contribution into the Physical Truth
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The concept of inflective space is given. The topological properties of inflective spaces may add new perspectives to the physical truth. Inflective spaces have some specifications that give information may has a role to design physical universes. Inflective balls are defined as builders of physical universes. An inflective ball builds a universe in mesh structures and in infinite number of forms. Inflective balls have abilities like physical things and physical things cause inflective balls and vice versa iff specific conditions are provided. These specific conditions are related to forming and deforming processes. Physical things deform ingredients of their spaces. These deformations cause inflective domains. Inflective deformations of space regions cause physical effects. Both of cylindrically and/or spherically inflective spaces are studied by using inflective coordinates family.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Virtual Array Dual Band Loop Quasi – Yagi Antenna Design for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, numerical and experimental analyses of both dual band loop Quasi - Yagi Antenna and miniaturized virtual array of the same structure are studied. These both design operates at free band (2.4-2.48 GHz) and planned 5G mobile communication band (3.4-3.8 GHz). Here, by introducing the virtual array concept, comparison between single element and the array structure are done. Proposed design is validated by High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) and also measurements for each antennas are carried out on fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: Causal Dynamic Constitutive Relations for Lossy Dispersive Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The relationship between a polarization vector and an electric field applied to a lossy dielectric media of Lorentz type is considered in a novel format of Maxwell’s equations. Dynamic processes are studied via solving Newton’s equation of motion for the polarization vector, where a given applied electric field stands at its right-hand side as a force term. The applied field can have a beginning and an end in time. The causal solution is obtained via solving the motion equation by the method of matrix exponential. Two examples are exhibited where the problem is solved explicitly in the class of the real-valued functions of time.

articleTitle: Electroquasistatic and Magnetoquasistatic Equations and Fields
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Maxwellian differential equations are derived for the near scattered fields of electrically small perfect electric conductors (PEC's) illuminated by time-domain incident electromagnetic fields. These "electroquasistatic" and "magneto-quasistatic" equations and fields are shown to become exact as the electrical size of the scatterer approaches zero.

articleTitle: Stochastic Sensitivity Analysis of Bioheat Transfer Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents the stochastic model of the bioheat transfer equation to assess the temperature distribution in the biological tissue. This is an important issue in planning and modeling of biomedical applications of electromagnetic (EM) fields such as EM HyperThermia (EM HT) procedures used in the treatment of certain cancer types. The presented approach aims to incorporate the uncertainties in the tissue thermal parameters aiming to quantify the uncertainty in the output temperature. The novel stochastic collocation method is implemented to estimate the stochastic mean and variance, as well as, to carry out the sensitivity analysis of model. The obtained results are the first step and a sort of an opener for the full stochastic modeling of EM HT.

articleTitle: Investigating Multiple Diffractions Near Optical Boundaries with Bidirectional Ray-Tracing and Antenna Reciprocity
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The antenna transfer function in multiple knife-edge diffraction scenarios is characterized with the bidirectional ray-tracing method. The receiving and the transmitting antennas are located near or at the optical boundaries where the traditional Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) solution fails in terms of accuracy. The new algorithm overcomes the accuracy issues of UTD where both transmitter and receiver antennas are utilized for ray launching. The rays are captured on a large interaction surface and the transfer function is computed by evaluating the reciprocity integral over this surface. The simulation results are compared to the Vogler method, which is used as reference, and the merits of the bidirectional ray-tracing in terms of accuracy are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Wireless Power Transfer and Dual Ultrahigh-Frequency Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper is presenting a hybrid system including a high frequency (HF) coil and a dual Ultra High-Frequency (UHF) antenna for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) applications. The coils' operating frequencies are 510 MHz, and the antennas work at 2.48 GHz and 4.66 GHz. The system was designed and fabricated on FR4 substrates. The antennas can be used for power transfer or communication. One of the current challenges for wireless power transfer for small sensors is to minimize the system size. By proposing small size antennas that are integrated with the coils we are aiming to address this issue.

articleTitle: Extension of Snoek’s Law to Higher RF Frequencies by Controlling Nanomagnetic Particle Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Snoek's law is one of the key theories to describe the relationship between the permeability level and the operating frequency in the bulk ferromagnetic material. Generalized Snoek's law, proposed by Acher et al., introduced the integral form to investigate the high frequency properties of ferromagnetic films and composites. In this paper, we study the influence of the size and shape on the properties of nanometer-scale magnetic particles (nanomagnets). It is shown that the size, thickness and geometric shape of nanomagnets play a vital role in determining the magnetic properties. However, they are still governed by either Snoek's law or generalized Snoek's law. Micromagnetic software package, Object Oriented MicroMagnetic Framework (OOMMF) is used as a theoretical framework in this study. Understanding the influence of shape opens the way to designing new nanostructured magnetic materials where the magnetic properties can be tailored to a particular application.

articleTitle: A Novel Modified Silicon Micromachining Process with Near-Zero Dielectric Loss for High-Efficiency Antenna Design up to Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel modified silicon micromachining process is proposed to design high radiation efficiency antennas from microwave to terahertz band. By utilizing the proposed process, the air-filled structures can be introduced to mitigate the dielectric loss. As an example, slot antenna array is presented by periodically adding blocking structures to suppress the opposite fringing electric field of transmission line. The antenna array is fabricated using the proposed near-zero dielectric loss process and tested. The results show that by using the proposed process, the radiation efficiency is up to 90% even in terahertz band, much higher than conventional silicon process, i.e., 30%~40%. Moreover, considering the silicon MEMS process, the achieved antennas are with potential in system-on-chip applications.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Incident Field Dosimetry for GSM Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper provides some measured and calculated results for the electric field radiated by a base station antenna for GSM technology. Three different models have been used for the electric field assessment: Free Space approximation, Fresnel plane wave approach and Modified Image Theory Method (MIT) approach. Measured field values have been extrapolated to the maximum traffic scenario and compared to estimated field values.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Origami Dual Frequency Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A major component of any communication or wireless sensor is an antenna. There is interest in developing multifunctional and reconfigurable antennas that can morph into different shapes and provide different functionalities. The interest of using one antenna for multiple purposes is usually due to limitations of size and weight, and the increasing need for wireless devices such as wireless power transfer, communication and wireless sensors. Some of the challenges to overcome include having a small form factor, being low-cost and robust, and providing high gain. In this work we are presenting an origami inspired hexagonal shape antenna array. Origami is the art of paper folding and the basis of origami method can be used to design antennas that can be folded and unfold based on deployment need. For example, Kimonis et. al. [1] proposed a power-harvesting cube with the antennas made using inkjet printing. The shape memory hinges are used to change the cube to a flat shape. Another example is the use of a 3D printing method by Shah and Lim [2]. In this paper they designed a push/pull method to change the shape of the array. The initial results of the basic hexagonal antenna elements needed to reconfigure form 2.4 GHz to 5.8 GHz are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Millimeter-Wave Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The congested sub-65GHz spectrum has steered the attention towards millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communication systems. To date, mm-wave systems have either sacrificed efficiency, bandwidth, or cost to be realized. In this paper, we present a low cost wideband feed for UWB Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) operating across Ku-K-Ka bands and 5G bands (viz. 17.5-70 GHz) with emphasis on dual linear polarization. The presented array and feed are packaged in a compact profile (H = 2.7 mm) suitable for mobile and hand-held devices. Notably, the novelty of this antenna is the use of low-cost standard PCB processes, with Ball Grid Array (BGA) connection for a radiation efficient System in Package (SiP) approach. The presented mm-wave TCDA achieves over 52 GHz of instantaneous bandwidth for VSWR <; 3 with scanning down to 60° in both E and H planes in infinite array simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Axial Corrugated Ka-band Feed Horn
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: antenna radiation patterns; electromagnetic wave scattering; optical metamaterials; antenna arrays; electromagnetic wave polarisation; Green's function methods; UHF antennas; Maxwell equations; optical design techniques; antenna feeds.

articleTitle: Teaching Electromagnetics and Antennas Using Free Software and Online Calculators
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Teaching Electromagnetics can be made more exciting to students when there are hands-on experiments. Although in-class laboratories can be set up with well-established commercial software, there are challenges such as costs and maintenance of licenses, which make them inapplicable to some instructors. This paper presents several free software and online calculators that allow an instructor to set up low-cost and reliable electromagnetics and antennas laboratories.

articleTitle: Application of The Method of Fractional Derivatives to the Solution of the Problem of Plane Wave Diffraction by Two Axisymmetric Strips of Different Sizes
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we have considered the problem of plane wave diffraction by two strips. This structure is an open resonator which consists of two axisymmetric strips of different widths. The application of the Fractional Derivative (FDM) method allows one to obtain a general solution, which, as a particular case, contains, for fractional order (FO) values α equal, α = 0 and, α = 1 the solution of the problem when the strips are perfectly electrically conductive (PEC, = 0) and perfectly magnetically conductive (PMC, α = 1). For values of the FO from the interval α ∈ (0,1), we have a resonator in which the conductivity of the mirrors is intermediate between the PEC and the PMC.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a W-Band Circular Polarized Feed Horn with Inbuilt Polarizer for Low f/D Offset Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A novel W-band left-hand circular polarized (LHCP) cylindrical waveguide feed horn antenna is proposed. The circular polarized wave is generated in the internal polarizer structure by 9 pairs of circular cavities, eliminating the need for an orthomode transducer or a complex septum. The proposed horn antenna's dimension is 26 mm × 14 mm × 5.25 mm. The antenna has impedance matching (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -15 dB) and axial ratio below 1.2 dB from 79.5 GHz to 88 GHz. The horn is used as a feed source for an offset parabolic reflector of 10 cm diameter and low f/D ratio 0.25. The measurement of the prototyped feed horn and the offset parabolic reflector antenna validates the analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: Range-Doppler and Radar Cross Section Routines of a Circularly Distributed Array
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Ensemble progressions for the sophisticated array factors of range-Doppler routines and radar cross sections of simulated scan behavior are investigated and compared against theoretical derivations for a circularly planar distributed array. This topology distribution is attractive because of its mathematical ease of analysis and is bound to a maximum aperture radius A.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Analysis of Small Group Target
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The radar cross section (RCS) of a group target, composed of multiple scatterer elements, can be found approximately through array composition of the RCS of each element. In order to verify the validity of the pertinent method, this paper compares results obtained through array composition and numerical calculation for RCS in the case where an aircraft scatterers model constitute a small group target. In addition, the relationship is examined between the spacing of elements composing the group target, and coupling between elements. The results showed that coupling decreased with increasing element spacing, and if the element spacing is sufficiently large, RCS of the entire group target can be found with good precision through array composition.

articleTitle: RF Effects of Umbrella Reflector Antenna Topology for CubeSats: Optimal Feed Point, Boresight Gain Loss and Grating Lobes
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The development of compact high gain antennas for Cube-Sats can enable several advanced space missions at lower costs, and is an active area of research within the antenna community. A special class of reflector antenna, known as the umbrella reflector has regained much interest due to its ability to meet the demands of advanced space missions that require high gain and/or high spatial resolution. The umbrella reflector surface consists of a finite number of parabolic ribs, which are connected through surfaces called gores, which deviate from the true parabolic shape. This causes the radiation performance of the umbrella reflector surface to be far less intuitive than the conventional paraboloid. In this work, we provide a comprehensive understanding of the radiation mechanism of the umbrella reflector. We describe the techniques that have been investigated to determine the optimum feed position, study the dependency of the gain on the diameter and number of ribs and analyze the appearance of far-field grating lobes. Several closed form expressions are derived to aid the design of umbrella reflectors and achieve the tradeoff between mechanical complexity and RF performance.

articleTitle: The MTM-EBG: A Fully Uniplanar, Printable, and Embedded Solution for Multi-Band Functionality in Microstrip Devices and Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This work reviews applications of the recently developed metamaterial-based electromagnetic bandgap structure (MTM-EBG) to provide multi-band behavior in printed microwave circuit devices. Developed rigorously using multiconductor transmission line theory, the MTM-EBG is well-modeled, uniplanar, and can be embedded directly into existing microstrip structures, making it suitable for a variety of devices. The theory of operation is discussed and a summary of recently developed MTM-EBG-based multi-band devices is presented, with relevant results compiled for each. The included multi-band structures range from modified microstrip circuit devices to patch antennas, which demonstrate the versatility and broad applicability of the MTM-EBG.

articleTitle: Transient impedance of the horizontal grounding electrode: Sensitivity analysis of the direct time domain analytical solution
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper deals with the statistical analysis of the impact various parameters (electrode length, soil conductivity and permittivity) can have on the value of transient impedance of the horizontal grounding electrode. Deterministic model for the transient impedance calculation is based on the corresponding Pocklington integro-differential equation in the frequency domain for the calculation of induced current and Generalized Telegrapher's Equation for the calculation of the scattered voltage. These equations are solved using previously developed analytical techniques, thus obtaining transient impedance directly in the time domain. Stochastic collocation method is applied by taking into account random parameters and performing subsequent sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: Analytic Description of the Coherence Properties of High Frequency Field in the Inhomogeneous Stochastic Transionospheric Channel with Anisotropic Random Irregularities
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Explicit analytical results are presented which permit analyzing the coherence properties of the high-frequency field propagating through the stochastic transionospheric channel with the inhomogeneous background ionosphere and anisotropic random inhomogeneities of the electron density.

articleTitle: Exact Geometrical Optics Scattering by a 45° Metal Wedge Illuminated by Multiple Plane Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A perfectly conducting metal wedge whose aperture angle is equal to a quarter of π radian is considered. It is shown that if the primary field consists of seven plane waves with appropriate amplitude, phase and direction of incidence, then the edge of the wedge does not scatter and the geometrical optics field is the exact, closed-form solution to the boundary-value problem.

articleTitle: Perfect Anomalous Reflection and Refraction Accompanied by an Ideal Polarization Conversion: Potential of a Chiral Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Electrically thin layers, composed of sub-wavelength-size inclusions known as metasurfaces, are exploited to shape the wavefront of electromagnetic waves. In this work, we engineer ideal polarization rotator metasurfaces which perfectly reflects or refracts a normally illuminated electromagnetic plane wave into an anomalous direction. Our approach is based on applying boundary conditions to relate the induced electric and magnetic equivalent dipole polarizations per unit-cell to the jump of both electric and magnetic fields at the metasurface boundary, and to find the required electric and magnetic polarization densities, and finally to allocate a desired topology to achieve the aforementioned goals of anomalous scattering. We use an analytical model and demonstrate that such design realizations are achievable using metasurfaces with scatterers possessing a chiral topology.

articleTitle: Seamless Waveguide Bends with In-Line Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present a synthesis scheme for metasurfaces (MS) for perfect transmission of waveguided modes through sharp bends in rectangular metallic waveguides (WG). Uncommonly, the MS is utilized as an in-line component, placed at the bend discontinuity. The inherent symmetry of the configuration allows retaining the modal integrity while locally conserving the power across the MS, facilitating passive lossless design via previously developed analytical methods. Verified using full-wave simulations, this approach is found to yield unitary transmission efficiency across the bend, laying the ground for future explorations of WG-integrated MSs for mode manipulation.

articleTitle: Modeling Metamaterial Element in Dielectric-filled Waveguide-fed Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We study the modeling of metamaterial elements etched into planar, dielectric-filled waveguides for metasurface antennas. Metamaterial elements in these devices are subwavelength-sized, resonant openings embedded in waveguide walls-that can be modeled as the electric and magnetic dipoles-and couple to waveguide modes and radiate into free space. Due to a dielectric filling the waveguide, the dipole moments representing the element can contribute unequally to the scattered fields into the waveguide and the radiated fields into free space. Such different dipole strengths need to be considered for analytic modeling of metasurfaces. In this work, we present a retrieval of dipole moments of a metamaterial element by applying the law of power conservation and demonstrate its utility in the analytic model for the metasurface antennas.

articleTitle: Using the Power Transfer Efficiency for RFID detection in Unusual Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The increasing number of RFID applications has given rise to practical issues that deserve specific attention and analysis. In particular, the detection of UHF RFID tags in scenarios where usual propagating models such as ray tracing or free-space propagation are not applicable have been described and analyzed, highlighting that novel performance parameters such as Power Transfer Efficiency must be introduced.

articleTitle: A Novel Semi-Analytical Mode-Matching Technique for Modeling Realistic Electromagnetic Well-Logging Sensors Immersed in Dissipative Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel formulation to model electromagnetic logging while drilling (LWD) sensors immersed in dissipative inhomogeneous geophysical formations. We analyze the electromagnetic boundary problem via the mode-matching technique and then use such results as a basis for modeling the complex-valued input impedance of the antennas employed in realistic LWD tools. Numerical simulations are presented to validate this approach.

articleTitle: Recent Contributions to Multiobjective Evolutionary Optimization in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEAs) have provided engineers with powerful new tools for rapidly designing highly complex electromagnetic systems. This paper serves as a brief tutorial on optimization in electromagnetics (EM), and also surveys three recent contributions to the field of MOEAs, each of which have expanded the space of optimizable designs in different ways.

articleTitle: Applications and Potentials of Reciprocal Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We review different applications and potentials of reciprocal bianisotropic metasurfaces including uniform and gradient metasurfaces, in particular, with anisotropic, chiral, and omega properties. Based on an analytic analysis, we discuss the necessary conditions to observe asymmetric co-and cross- polarization reflection and/or transmission, polarization conversion and rotation, asymmetric absorption, etc. We consider two kinds of incident wave scenarios based on linear and circular polarization.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Output Power Minimization Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to an antenna system to minimize an output power. The antenna system consists of a 2×2 antenna array and phase shifters which are controlled by a microcontroller. PSO algorithm is implemented to choose the best setup of the four phase shifters to null the high-power signals (jammers) and allow reception of the desired signals.

articleTitle: A Note on Measures of Human Exposure to Signals with Continuous Spectra
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper deals with measures for evaluating the human exposure to signals with continuous spectra, such as signals radiated from power line communication systems (PLC), ground penetrating radar (GPR), or other ultra-wideband signals. A new approach is proposed, arising from the signal theory, where integrals of radiated field spectra are calculated from the measured field amplitudes. A computational example is presented, which deals with PLC signals; future work will deal with GPR signals.

articleTitle: Location of Surface Wave Poles in Sommerfeld type Integrals: A Mittag-Leffler Expansion Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, the Mittag-Leffler (ML) expansion method is introduced to find surface and leaky wave poles. The ML expansion method replaces the trigonometric functions present in Sommerfeld type integrals with equivalent expansion functions. One of the many applications is to solve for multilayered media Green's functions that are needed to calculate currents on microstrip patch antennas and interconnects. The ML expansion method has been applied and tested on microstrip problems with various dielectric permittivities, for electrically thick and thin substrates and for lossless and lossy cases.

articleTitle: Maxwell’s View of Electric Polarization as Displacement
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: After reconfirming that all the equations that today are commonly referred to as Maxwell's equations are found in Maxwell's Treatise, we show from his Treatise that Maxwell considered his displacement D as the electric polarization and did not introduced in his Treatise or papers the concept of electric polarization P or the polarization volume and surface charge densities, -∇· P and n̂· P. With this realization, we show that Maxwell's discussion of surface charge density between volume elements of dielectrics and conductors becomes understandable.

articleTitle: TM-wave propagation in a graded waveguide structure
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We investigate TM-wave propagation in a hollow waveguide with a graded dielectric layer, described using a hyperbolic tangent function. General formulae for the electric field components of the TM-waves, applicable to hollow waveguides with arbitrary cross sectional shapes, are presented. We derive the analytical results for the reflection and transmission coefficients valid for waveguides of arbitrary cross sectional shapes. Thereby, we show that the obtained reflection and transmission coefficients are in exact asymptotic agreement with those obtained for a very thin homogeneous dielectric layer using mode-matching and cascading. The proposed method is tractable since it gives analytical results that are directly applicable without the need of mode-matching, and it has the ability to model realistic, smooth transitions.

articleTitle: Semi-Active Multiple Beam Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The low power efficiency (5-15%) of solid state power amplifiers, working in back-off to guarantee a good linearity, could become the show stopper for some future space and terrestrial communication ventures at Ka-band and above. Semi-active reflector and conformal antennas, using Butler-like matrices between the power amplifiers and the feed elements, were first introduced to directly generate flexible multiple beams most efficiently.For linear and planar arrays, such phase-only control at power amplifier inputs can provide beam zooming or amplitude tapering, but no proper beam steering. The paper discusses and analyses the extension of the semi-active principle to linear and planar arrays, by use of multiport amplifiers with amplitude and phase input control to power the elements most efficiently.Performances and limitations of such systems are analyzed and demonstrated for a few examples.

articleTitle: Boundary Value Problems for the Bi-Anisotropic Maxwell System in Lipschitz Domains
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The initial boundary value problem for the time dependent Maxwell system under bi-anisotropy in a non-smooth domain (a cavity) is analyzed. It is shown that this problem is well-posed provided the material parameters satisfy certain coercivity assumptions. Minimal smoothness of these parameters and time independent boundary data belonging to an appropriate Sobolev space is imposed to obtain existence of classical solutions. Finally, we address the free space problem.

articleTitle: Propagation over an arbitrary constant impedance plane for arbitrary primary sources, exact series and complete asymptotics with error functions
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present here a compact solution for the electromagnetic field scattered by an arbitrary constant impedance plane (passive or active), considering exact potentials for arbitrary primary current sources. The special function involved in our expressions are rewritten with non-singular integral expression, for which we derive exact series and complete asymptotics, both expressed in terms of error functions.

articleTitle: Design of Optical Waveguide Devices Using Function-Expansion-Based Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we study on the function-expansion-based topology optimization method for an efficient design of optical waveguide devices. In our approach, a refractive index distribution in the design region is expressed by using function expansion method, the finite element method (FEM) is used to calculate propagating behavior in optical waveguide devices, and the adjoint variable method (AVM) is employed to efficiently evaluate sensitivities for the gradient-based optimization.

articleTitle: A High-Frequency Uniform Asymptotic Solution for Electromagnetic Field Scattering by a 3D Wedge Including Grazing Incidence Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper we present a modified version of the uniform asymptotic theory of diffraction (UAT) for 3D wedge scattering that generalizes former approaches to render correct field solutions in grazing incidence scenarios. We present numerical results that show the proposed method is asymptoticly uniform up to convenient orders of accuracy as in the UAT approach, but with the advantage that continues valid when the incident wave becomes parallel to one of the wedge faces.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of High Frequency Fields on Transionospheric Paths along Strongly Anisotropic Random Inhomogeneities of Electron Density
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Two methods for description of the effects of propagation through a quasi-random spatial distribution of the electron density in the ionosphere are further tried. The special case of propagation of a high frequency wave field in the direction of strongly elongated random inhomogeneities is considered. Comparison of the results of solving the same propagation problem employing different techniques is performed, and the range of validity is discussed.

articleTitle: The Role of the Steepest-Descent Path in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The steepest-descent path (SDP) is a valuable tool in electromagnetics for analyzing the physical significance of guided-wave modes in a variety of situations, and also for asymptotically predicting the behavior of the fields on a guiding structure when excited by a source. This presentation will overview some of the applications of the SDP in electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Textile-Based Ultra-Wideband Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: There is an emerging potential concerning textile electronics that combine the comfort, flexibility, and durability of textiles, with the functionality, connectivity, and intelligence of electronics. In this regard, the implementation of an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna on textile will bring the advantages of a multi-functional system to a structure that will allow for a range of compressible/stretchable operations. In this paper, we present, for the first time, a low profile and low-cost UWB Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) on a textile (i.e denim) substrate. A full-wave simulation of an infinite array, complete with textile and conductive thread characteristics, shows VSWR <; 3 for scanning down to 60° from boresight in both E and H planes across a 6.5:1 bandwidth (0.9 GHz - 5.85 GHz). A near-theoretical realized gain value was also analyzed across the whole operating band.

articleTitle: A 2D/Q-2D Subdomain Finite Element Method for Irregular Power/Ground Plate-Pair Analysis with Waveport Excitation
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The field distribution of a power/ground plane can be fully characterized by TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">zmn</inf> modes, where the electric fields have both azimuthal and longitudinal components and the magnetic fields have only the azimuthal component. Thus, if the magnetic fields are defined to be the unknowns in the finite element method (FEM) used for the analysis of the power/ground plane structure, the analysis becomes a quasi-two dimensional (Q-2D) problem. Since the high-order modes are evanescent, they are tightly confined to the near region of the vias guarded by anti-pads; while in the regions sufficiently far from the anti-pads, only the fundamental mode should be accounted for. Therefore, the Q-2D problem is naturally transformed to be a hybrid 2D and Q-2D one. Compared with the brute-force three dimensional (3D) analysis, the number of unknowns is significantly reduced. To further reduce the computational cost, a new Riemann solver inspired domain decomposition method (D-DM), which accounts for the 2D and Q-2D region separately, is further proposed. The numerical flux for the Maxwell equations are used to realize the information exchange between the two domains. Finally, numerical examples are given to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-Focal Metalenses Based on Complete Decoupling of Amplitude, Phase and Polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The simultaneous control of amplitude and phase via metasurfaces affords us unprecedented degree of freedom in manipulating electromagnetic waves, but currently most designs suffer from low efficiency which raises certain concerns for real-world applications. Moreover, the complete amplitude, phase and polarization modulation is particularly challenging, which typically requires a combination of attenuators, optically thick wave plates and large dielectric lenses. Here, we propose an alternative scheme by introducing vertical mode cross-coupling for polarization control and high efficiency, while by involving spatially-varied orientations and structures for independent amplitude and phase modulation. The vertical mode cross-coupling is synthesized by stacking triple-layer twisted split ring resonators (SRRs) operated in transmissive scheme. Such tight cross-coupling and chirality-assisted coherent multiple resonances facilitates high cross-polarization conversion efficiency (~100%) and broadband transmission window with full phase cover. As a proof of concept, two dual-focal metalenses that are challenging to be actualized through conventional metasurfaces are designed, numerically and experimentally studied with a total thickness of λo/12 at microwave frequencies. Desirable dual focusing behavior with axial and lateral alignment of two foci are demonstrated. Our findings, not confined to microwave operation, opens up an alternative way in fine controlling light and can stimulate novel and high-performance versatile photonic metadevices.

articleTitle: Well-posedness of Scattering Problems at Luminal Space-Time Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present a method to calculate the scattering of a wave from an interface propagating with a velocity close to the speed of light. This is a problem that is ill-posed despite it being a direct problem. To our knowledge, this problem, despite its pervasiveness in technology, has been solved only numerically or by analytical discretization. Here, we suggest an alternate method to obtain closed-form solutions. The idea is to first solve the problem of a double interface, which is well-posed, and then introduce some loss between the two interfaces. This unambiguously provides the scattered wave coefficients for a single interface.

articleTitle: All-Dielectric Compact Superstrates for High-Gain Resonant-Cavity Antennas: Designs & Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents the designs and measurements of two compact single-layer all-dielectric resonant-cavity antennas (RCAs). Both the antennas are compact (footprint <; 5.5λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) and low in profile (overall height <; 0.9λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>). The first RCA consists of a single-layer partially reflecting superstrate (PRS) in which thickness and permittivity vary from the center towards the edge of the PRS. Four commercially available dielectric materials are used to achieve this permittivity variation. This RCA demonstrates a measured peak directivity of 20.7 dBi and its 3dB directivity bandwidth extends from 12.75-19 GHz, which is 57% at the center frequency. The second RCA, made out of a single dielectric material demonstrates a measured peak directivity of 20.3 dBi and its measured 3dB directivity bandwidth is 55.9%. This class of compact single-layer RCAs, with a directivity bandwidth product per unit area (DBP/A) of greater than 1200, successfully overcomes the trade-off between directivity, bandwidth, profile and footprint and breaks the challenging barrier that has existed for RCAs over the last decade (and other planar high-gain antennas).

articleTitle: New Propagation Regimes of TM Waves in a Waveguide filled with a Nonlinear Dielectric Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We consider propagation of surface TM waves in a circular metal-dielectric waveguide filled with nonlinear (Kerr nonlinearity) metamaterial medium. Analysis is reduced to solving a nonlinear transmission eigenvalue problem for an ordinary differential equation; eigenvalues of the problem correspond to propagation constants of the surface waves. For the numerical solution, a method is proposed based on solving an auxiliary Cauchy problem (a version of the shooting method). As a result of comprehensive numerical modeling, new propagation regimes are discovered.

articleTitle: Modeling Intermittency of Scintillating Transionospheric Signals
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper investigates the statistical characteristics of the field in the fluctuating transionospheric channel of propagation with intermittency effects taken into account. The intermittency of the ionospheric turbulence is introduced through utilizing the non-Gaussian multifractal stochastic distribution of irregularities of the electron density. As a result of scattering on the intermittent structures, the realizations of the scattered field also reveal intermittent behavior. The propagation problem is simulated utilizing the random screen technique. The statistical characteristics of the field fluctuations after passing the phase screen are studied, and the peculiarities of the field statistics due to the non-Gaussianity of the screen are demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: L-Band Wide-Angle Circular Polarized Sequential Rotated Antenna for GPS Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A novel wide-angle circular polarized sequential rotated antenna element is proposed at L-band for GPS applications. The proposed antenna exhibits symmetric radiation patterns for the principal as well as diagonal planes at 1.575 GHz. In addition, it provides a high front-to-back ratio, low cross polarization, and wide axial ratio beamwidth. Right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) with an axial ratio (AR) less than 3 dB is maintained over the wide angle. This antenna is advantageous for communication systems that require wider circularly polarized coverage and gain performance.

articleTitle: The Fredholm Factorization in Presence of Penetrable Rectangular Rods
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The Fredholm factorization of the Wiener Hopf equations is extended to study planar stratified regions in presence of impenetrable and/or penetrable rectangular cylinders. The general theory requires to consider several aspects of the Wiener Hopf technique. In order to illustrate it with an example, in this paper we limit the analysis to the diffraction by a dielectric rectangular rod lying on a PEC plane.

articleTitle: Green Function Methods for Optoelectronics
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We discuss implementation of Green function methods to simulation of transport and optical response (fluxes, noise and noise spectrum) in molecular junctions. We indicate deficiencies in standard tools of nonlinear optical spectroscopy when applied to open molecular systems, and suggest suitable alternatives based on many-body flavors of the nonequilibrium Green function method.

articleTitle: OTA Experiments on the Angular Accuracy of a Phase Monopulse AOA Antenna Using the Mean IQ-Value Method in a Rician Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we conduct investigations on the angular accuracy of a circularly arranged phase monopulse Angle of Arrival (AOA) estimation antenna in Rician multipath propagation environments. A novel algorithm, called the mean IQ-value method (MIQ method), is presented to extract true angular information about incident waves in a Rician fading channel, where the received signal is therefore composed of both random multipath scattered fields and a coherent line-of-sight (LOS) component. The experimental results using an Over-The-Air (OTA) fading emulator show that a high accuracy of angle estimation can be achieved using the proposed MIQ method, even in the case of a severe Rician fading channel, where a LOS component is extremely small, such as a Rice factor of K = -10 dB.

articleTitle: Simple and Insightful Computation of Space-Time Crystal Dispersion Diagrams
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper provides tools to sketch the dispersion diagram of space-time crystals. These tools are the reciprocal lattice vector and the average phase velocity. The latter is given in closed form for the first time to our knowledge. This work offers new insight into the physics of space-time crystals.

articleTitle: Surface Electromagnetics: Historic Development and Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of surface electromagnetics, an emerging area for electromagnetic phenomena occurring on natural or engineered surfaces. It includes a review on historic development of various EM surfaces, followed by representative examples in antenna engineering.

articleTitle: On the optimal plasmonic resonances in gold nanospheres embedded in dispersive media
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: New fundamental upper bounds have recently been given regarding the optimal plasmonic multipole resonances of a rotationally invariant sphere embedded in a lossy surrounding medium. The new theory is based on a generalized optical theorem for the absorption of a sphere in a lossy medium and employs straightforward analysis to explicitly maximize a concave function. The new bounds are briefly summarized in this paper and then employed in a study concerning the effectiveness of using gold nanospheres as absorbers of the sizes typically used in biomedical applications and plasmonic photothermal therapy.

articleTitle: Spectral Numerical Green’s Function Based Eigenanalysis for Cavity Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Efficient eigenanalyses are proposed for cavities which are geometrically or materially perturbed. The method leverages the spectral representation of the numerical Green’s function (NGF) of the unperturbed cavity system. The convergence of the series formed by resonant solenoidal modes is accelerated by performing an NGF extraction at one low wavenumber. With spectral NGFs, this approach gives rise to small, linear matrix eigenvalue problems without the generation of spurious DC modes.

articleTitle: Metasurface Cloaks for Decoupling Closely Spaced Phased Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Here, we propose to apply the concept of electromagnetic invisibility/cloaking for decoupling two closely spaced antenna arrays operating at neighboring frequencies. Array elements used here are strip monopole antennas covered by previously designed conformal and confocal elliptical metasurface cloaks. We demonstrate that by cloaking two closely spaced antenna elements in strongly coupled antenna arrays enables to decouple the entire arrays in the near-field and in the far-field. The simulation results of two overlapping linear arrays operating at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> = 2.95 GHz and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 3.35 GHz are provided as examples.

articleTitle: Analytical Formulation for Loop Antennas Valid from the RF to Optical Regime: A Review
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Loop antennas are among one of the simplest antennas to construct. Yet, despite this fact, the mathematical complexity of the associated radiation integrals has complicated the understanding and modelling of such structures. Recently, a full analytical theory for the radiation properties of loop antennas has been derived, which is able to bridge this gap and provide a basis for better understanding the behavior of these antennas across all frequency ranges. Further, these models have been extended to include the effects of loading and coupling, as well as have revealed interesting properties such as superdirectivity by enabling rapid parametric studies and optimizations to be carried out.

articleTitle: Design of Chaotic Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Deforming the geometry of a rectangular reverberation chamber (RC) improves the field disorder and the chaoticity of the RC field, even in presence of traditional stirring mechanisms. We study how position and number of hemispherical wall diffractors affect the transmission-based modal overlapping of a real life RC facility. Numerical full wave finite-difference time-domain simulations were performed in order to evaluate the average field transmission over a broad frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: Manipulating Surface Waves and Nanoscale Forces/Torques with Nonreciprocal Platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the potential of nonreciprocal platforms to control and enhance surface waves and nanoscale forces/torques in unconventional ways. We consider a gyrotropic magnetized plasma as a model system that can be designed to exhibit either weak or strong forms of nonreciprocity, as well as elliptical or hyperbolic modal dispersion. We show that this continuum material platform supports ultra-narrow unidirectional surface-plasmon-polariton beams, tunable via the emitter operational frequency or the cyclotron frequency of the biased plasma. In addition, we also investigate the effect of launching such unidirectional surface modes on the emitter itself. We show that, due to the asymmetric release of angular momentum, a non-trivial optical torque is exerted a generic dipolar emitter. We obtain a closed-form expression for this optical torque in terms of the system Green function valid for any three-dimensional, inhomogeneous, dissipative, dispersive, nonreciprocal, and bianisotropic structure. Advanced material platforms of this type may provide new degrees of freedom to control the orientation and rotation of nano-objects and optically-driven rotary nanomachines.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antennas, Overcoming Deficiencies and Realizing Unexpected Performances
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The historical development of microstrip patch antenna is reviewed. It is indicated that it resulted from the problem of radiation loss in printed microstrip lines and microwave circuits, which deteriorated their performance. On the other hand, enhancing the radiation, developed it to be one of the most useful and dominant antennas in wireless communications and sensor applications. Its planar configuration is ideally suited for miniaturization and printed fabrication and has potential for further influence of the electronic device and communication technology advancements. The main steps in its development are highlighted and will be discussed in detail during the presentation.

articleTitle: Analogy Between Elastodynamic Displacement and Electromagnetic Vector Potentials
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This summary demonstrates a modeling analogy, for linear homogenous isotropic media, between the displacement vector u in elastodynamics e.g.(seismic) (ES) and the vector potential, either A or F, in electromagnetics (EM). This analogy will allow for EM modeling techniques to be used in the analysis of ES problems, and will also offer insight into the commonality of wave propagation in both domains. After developing the analogy, we present a simple example of its application to the classic example of an ES Love wave.

articleTitle: 100 years of Electromagnetic Waves in Random Media
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper gives a summary of the key research developments of electromagnetic waves in random media during the past 100 years, emphasizing the statistical multiple scattering theories applied to geophysical remote sensing and imaging of biological media by electromagnetic, optical, and ultrasound waves. This summary also includes considerations of integration of random media theories and signal processing. Radiative transfer theories have been extensively applied to remote sensing, imaging, and detection; recent developments include coherent effects in multiple scattering, acoustic multi-physics, and time-reversal imaging. This paper concludes with a discussion of possible future studies and research development.

articleTitle: Excitation of Eigenmode Current for Multiple Resonance Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this article, the condition on excitation fields achieving the multiple resonance of PEC spherical antenna is derived. The condition is transformed into the relationship of expansion coefficients of the vector spherical harmonics.

articleTitle: Quasi-static Design of Small Ultra-Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Electrostatic methods calculate the radiation resistance, capacitance and Q-factor ratio design curves for ultrawideband (UWB) monopoles. The lowest operating frequency is determined by the total electrostatic energy and the radiation resistance (Q-factor). Electrostatic methods with a line charge distribution were used to design the asymptotic conical dipole (ACD). This paper replaces the ACD line charge distribution with a charge distribution on a cone. The charge distribution on the cone is selected to give equipotential surfaces (monopole shapes) with conical feed points and top loads. Each charge distribution cone half-angle and cone length represents a unique monopole shape and also a point on the design curves. The 50 Ω and minimum Q-factor ratio monopole designs are selected from the Q-factor ratio design curve; then Maxwell's equations are numerically solved for the frequency range 30 MHz to 2.5 GHz. Minimizing the Q-factor ratio reduces the lowest operating frequency without increasing the voltage standing wave ratio of 1.2:1. This approach is a change from the "cut and try" method, where antenna shape is often arbitrarily selected and the Q-factor ratio is typically not used to select the antenna shape.

articleTitle: Forward and inverse homogenization of the electromagnetic properties of a quasiperiodic composite
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper deals with forward and inverse homogenization of Maxwell's equations with a geometry on a microscopic scale given by a quasiperiodic distribution of piece-wise constant components defined by the use of a mapping R : ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> → ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>, m > n, and a periodic unit cell in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. Inverse homogenization makes use of a Stieltjes analytic representation for the effective complex permittivity, which depends upon R, unlike for the periodic case.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf analysis of the diffraction by a half-plane dipole array
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present a rigorous solution to the canonical problem of the scattering by a semi-infinite planar array of dipoles, presenting an edge truncation, when illuminated by a plane wave. By applying the Wiener-Hopf technique to the Z-transformed system of equations derived from the electric field integral equation, we provide rigorous close form expressions for the current on the dipoles. We prove that such currents are the superposition of the infinite array Floquet-wave solution plus a perturbation, which comprises both edge diffraction and bound surface waves excited by the edge truncation.

articleTitle: Modern Applications of the Bateman-Whittaker Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The Bateman-Whittaker theory, which was developed more than a century ago, is shown to be a comprehensive basis for deriving a large class of null spatiotemporally localized waves characterized by intriguing vorticial structures. In addition, it provides the proper modeling for studying topological structures dealing with linked and knotted electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: 3D Printing-based Liquid Metal Patch Antennas with Wide-Band Frequency and Multi-Polarization Reconfigurations
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we present two reconfigurable patch antenna designs utilizing liquid metal tuning slots: a wide-band frequency reconfigurable patch antenna with frequency tuning bandwidth of 70% and instantaneous bandwidth of 2%; and a multi-polarization reconfigurable patch antenna with right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), left-hand circular polarization (LHCP), and linear polarization (LP) with arbitrary orientation in x-y plane. The design and prototype strategy developed in this paper can be applied to other potential topologies with various reconfigurable functionalities.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conformal Antennas With Quasi-Cylindrical Anisotropic Substrates Using Discrete Mode Matching Method
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper deals with the extension of the Discrete Mode Matching (DMM) method to analyze conformal microstrip antennas fabricated with quasi-cylindrical anisotropic substrates. The computation of the field components at the interfaces is done with the cylindrical coordinate system. A full-wave equivalent circuit (FWEC) is used to calculate the dyadic Green's function of the system. Spatial-domain formulation is used to smoothly interpret the conformal interface of the structure. The method is applied to compute S-parameters and input impedance of microstrip antennas with elliptical substrate.

articleTitle: From transformation optics to topology: local and global methods for material design
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: There are two basic approaches for designing electromagnetic materials. The first approach is local, where the field is manipulated at each point in space to achieve a desired goal: transformation optics is of this kind. The second approach is global, where e.g. an integral of the material parameters governs certain characteristics of a device. Methods of topology are of this second kind. In this talk I shall show some new design techniques of this second kind, from designing reflectionless media, to applications of topology to design one-way devices and graded index waveguides.

articleTitle: Angle of Incidence-Stable FSS with DSRS Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A thin screen FSS with the double square ring slot (DSRS) element is proposed and demonstrated for a dual band spatial filter exhibiting closely separated pass and stop bands. The calculated band-separation-ratio is 1.15. Further, the predicted FSS transmission performance shows excellent stability with the incident angle from normal to 45° and for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: Optical metasurfaces based on spheroidal nanoparticles: theory and applications
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Metasurfaces are revolutionizing the way we can control and manipulate light. Unprecedented functionalities, such as anomalous reflection and refraction, can be achieved using ultrathin surfaces textured at nanoscale. The aim of this contribution is reviewing our recent efforts in the development of analytical models able describing the response of some widely-used classes of optical metasurfaces. We show, both theoretically and through full-wave simulations, that arrays of spheroidal nanoparticles can be fully characterized relying on the surface impedance concept, and that the availability of such models enables the design of innovative optical devices and components.

articleTitle: A General Approach to the Analysis of Complex Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We propose a technique for the search and calculation of complex waves in open and shielded circularly symmetric metal-dielectric waveguides with piecewise homogeneous filling by proving the existence and determination of the location of roots of the corresponding dispersion equations in the complex domain. The approach develops the method employing generalized cylindrical polynomials applied earlier to the rigorous analysis and determination of real waves.

articleTitle: Non-passive approximation as a tool to study the realizability of amplifying media
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Non-passive approximation is presented as a tool to study the realizability of amplifying media. As an interesting physical example, we derive first a suitable approximation of the plasmonic singularity of a dielectric sphere with respect to a hypothetical amplifying background medium. A non-passive approximation based on convex optimization is then employed to investigate the necessary bandwidth requirements to achieve the approximate pole singularity.

articleTitle: Floquet-Bloch Analysis of a Practical Fabry-Perot Huygens’ Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Realization of the anomalous refraction effects predicted by Huygens' metasurfaces (HMS) have required tedious and time-consuming trial-and-error numerical full-wave computations. It is shown herein that these requirements can be alleviated for transverse magnetic (TM) propagation by a periodic dielectric-based HMS consisting of an array of Fabry-Perot etalons which mimic the local transmission coefficient of an abstract zero-thickness HMS (ZT-HMS).
